sanskrit: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये । मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥
hindiTranslation: और तो क्या कहूँ जितने भी सात्त्विक, राजस और तामस भाव हैं, वे सब मुझ से ही होते हैं  ऐसा समझो ।  पर मैं उनमें और वे मेरेमें नहीं हैं ॥
englishTranslation: Know that all states of being—sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic—arise from Me. I am not in them; they are in Me.
essence: All qualities arise in the divine, yet the divine is not bound by any of them.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Every mode of nature—clear, restless, or dull—comes from Krishna. But Krishna is beyond all of them and is not confined by any one quality.
simpleInsight: You can notice your moods without believing they define the deepest reality.
detailedMeaning: Krishna keeps unfolding the truth behind all experience. After naming his powers in the world, Krishna now says that every quality of mind and nature comes from him, yet he remains beyond those qualities.
modernRelevance: A retired schoolteacher is cheerful at breakfast, irritable by lunch and flat by evening, and calls each mood himself. Krishna places all three moods in nature, which comes from him, and stands beyond them.
translationLiteral: ये (which) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सात्त्विकाः (sattvic) / भावाḥ (states of being) / राजसाः (rajasic) / तामसाः (tamasic) / च (and) / ये (which) / मत्तः (from Me) / एव (indeed) / इति (thus) / तान् (them) / विद्धि (know) / न (not) / तु (but) / अहम् (I) / तेषु (in them) / ते (they) / मयि (in Me)
insight: Sattva, rajas and tamas all come from Krishna, he says, yet they rest in him and he stays beyond.

quoteVariants.text: All states arise from Me. I remain untouched by them.
They come from Me; I am beyond them.
Everything in you comes from Me, but I am not trapped there.
All qualities arise in Me, not I in them.
